description.narrative: The projects under the Pacific Resilience Program cover the activities in the following areas: Tonga, Marshall Islands, Vanuatu, Secretariat of the Pacific Community, and Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat. The objective for Tonga (P154840) is to strengthen early warning, resilient investments and financial protection of Tonga. The program components are: Strengthening Early Warning and Preparedness; Risk Reduction and Resilient Investments; Disaster Risk Financing; and Project and Program Management. The objectives for both Marshall Islands (P155257) and for Vanuatu (P155256) is to strengthen the financial protection of the Republic of Marshall Islands and Vanuatu. The program components are: Strengthening Early Warning and Preparedness; Risk Reduction and Resilient Investments; Disaster Risk Financing; and Project and Program Management. The objective of the Secretariat of the Pacific Community Pacific Resilience Program (P147839) and the Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat Pacific Resilience Program (P155542) is to strengthen early warning, resilient investments and financial protection of participating Pacific Islands and countries. The program components are: Strengthening Early Warning and Preparedness; Mainstreaming Risk Reduction and Resilient Investments; Disaster Risk Financing; and Project and Program Management.
To strengthen early warning and resilient investments of participating countries

title.narrative: Satisfaction of users with the early warning system

comment.narrative:
<p>Target exceeded.</p>

<p>It includes staff trained by the project from National Disaster Management Offices (NDMOs) in Tonga (9) and Samoa (7) who reported being satisfied with the early warning system (100%) in SPC’s end-of-project survey. The final&nbs;figure differs from the previous ISR due to the fact that SPC had previously included staff that were from other agencies outside of the NDMOs.</p>

<p>The wording and end target of this indicator was revised at restructuring in February 2021 to capture the total number of satisfied users rather than a percentage.</p>

title.narrative: Satisfaction of users with the early warning system
Hazard model for forecasting of impacts of extreme events operationalized

comment.narrative:
<p>Target achieved.</p>

<p>Impact-based forecasting operationalized in Samoa (as of October 2022) and Tonga (as of November 2023) and used for early warning. Forecasting includes (1) swell inundation; (2) tropical cyclone coastal inundation, (3) TC rainfall and (4) TC wind; (5) tsunami inundation; seasonal forecasts (up to 6 months) for: (6) swells and (7) tropical cyclone; (8) long-term climate forecast; and multi-hazard risk assessment (8) and (9) multi-hazard impact forecasting system. The system can yield detailed maps and expected annual damages resulting from the impact.</p>

<p>The wording and end target of this indicator was revised from 'Number of public assets with risk information available to inform resilient planning in targeted areas' at restructurng in February 2021 to better capture the impact-based forecasting systems being developed under the project. </p>

<p> </p>

title.narrative: Multi-hazard risk information systems strengthened and in use

comment.narrative:
<p>Target achieved.</p>

<p>The Pacific Resilience Nexus launched in August 2022. It consolidates 3,033 databases for disaster and climate related information from about 70 years of data. Expect to upload 25,000 layers of data over time.</p>

<p>The wording and end target of this indicator was revised at restructuring in February 2021 to better capture the broad data intended to be contained on the Nexus database.</p>

title.narrative: Number of personnel working in the disaster management area applying learned skills on the job

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>???????</strong>Target exceeded.</p>

<p>137 staff working in disaster risk management areas were trained by the project [Samoa (42), Tonga (45), Vanuatu (30), and RMI (20)] of which 85% (116) reported having applied learned skills to their job, according to SPC’s end-of-project survey. The final figure is slightly different to the previous figure recorded of 120 due to slightly different results from the final beneficiary surveys which were completed by SPC since the last ISR.</p>

<p>The wording and end target of this indicator was revised at restructuring in February 2021 to better capture the extent to which the knowledge gained from the trainings are applied in the workplace.</p>

title.narrative: Number of personnel working in the disaster management area applying learned skills on the job
Multi-hazard risk information systems strengthened and in use

comment.narrative:
<p>Target exceeded.</p>

<p>Beneficiaries were defined by the PAD as population in Samoa and Tonga who were able to receive timely and actionable hazard forecast and warning messages, understand the meaning and know what actions to take. Of the 137,704 total beneficiaries, 68,518 (almost 50%) were female. The original definition and end target remained the same throughout the project.</p>

<p>As of end-October 2023, Samoa reported 82,400 beneficiaries (of which 39,930 females) according to the indicator definition. Tonga estimated that 70% of the population of Tongatapu and ‘Eua (55,304 of which 28,588 females) were able to benefit from Impact Based Forecasting (IBF) as of early November 2023. Population numbers were taken from the 2021 census etrapolated to 2023 by the growth rates.  IBF warnings were transmitted by TV, AM radio, web, social media.</p>

Post disaster needs assessment undertaken and strengthened
Post disaster needs assessment undertaken and strengthened

comment.narrative:
<p>Target achieved.</p>

<p>The project trained 196 staff in post-disaster needs assessments (PDNAs) from the four participating PREP countries and hired five on-call PDNA experts (social/gender, infrastructure, water and sanitation, DRM and PDNA Coordinator) for the training. Damage assessments were carried out with trained PDNA experts in Vanuatu following twin cyclones in March 2023.</p>

p>This indicator was added during the project restructuring in February 2021 to capture and measure the reprioritised activity providing support for PDNAs to SPC member countries.</p>

title.narrative: High- Resolution Digital Elevation Model (DEM) developed and operationalized in target areas

comment.narrative:
<p>Target achieved.</p>

<p>LiDAR surveys were carried out in Vanuatu (coastal Tanna, Malekula and Efate islands) and in Tonga (Vava’u Island Group, Niuatoputapu Tafahi and ‘Eua Islands) covering 1,958 square km in Vanuatu and 1,001 square km&nbs;in Tonga. Based on the surveys, the project produced high resolution digital elevation models, hydro-enforced DEMs, and canopy height and building surface models that potentially support updated risk assessments in areas where one third of Vanuatu’s population lives, and in about one third of Tonga’s surface. The LiDAR products have been operationalized in Vanuatu, as early inputs to the Multi-Hazard Risk Assessments for Lenakel (Tanna) and Lakotoro (Malekula Island). LiDAR data for Tonga was delivered to Ministry of Natural Resources and it is expected to be used to expand IBF early warning products nationwide, for the expansion of Vava’u airport, for hydrographic maps for safe domestic shipping, coastal erosion estimates, and to estimate the volume of quarries’ aggregate extraction.   </p>

<p>This indicator was added during the project restructuring i n February 2021 to capture and measure the reprioritised activity on LiDAR data acquisition for Vanuatu and Tonga.</p>
